recommendation: Keep the audit commit as the FHIR-16148 reconciliation record. Future changes should require a new PA decision if they revisit Encounter.reason.value targets, repeat use cardinalities, or whether billing diagnosis ranking belongs on Account rather than Encounter.
issue_request: FHIR-16148 asked PA to clarify Encounter.reason and Encounter.diagnosis: reason should carry expected medical reasons or symptoms for the encounter, diagnosis should carry medical conditions addressed during the encounter, diagnosis/procedure billing ranking should move away from Encounter to Account, and new use value sets should include concepts such as Chief Complaint, Reason for Visit, Working, and Final.
initial_application: Source commit 084c723e14093f9463b52edae50c08bfd1194da5 explicitly names FHIR-16148 and applied the structural Encounter changes, examples, search parameters, and new encounter-reason-use and encounter-diagnosis-use terminology. A later combined-branch FHIR-38807 fix corrected stale Encounter prose that remained after that original application.
additional_context: Confluence page 51223352 identifies FHIR-16148 as the master tracker and records the approved no-rank Encounter design. Later final decisions explain current differences from the 2021 proposal: FHIR-38784 made reason.use and diagnosis.use repeat, FHIR-32130 added DiagnosticReport as an Encounter.reason target, FHIR-48869 left Encounter.reason.value references unchanged while synchronizing EpisodeOfCare, FHIR-19285 moved ranked billing diagnosis/procedure details to Account, and FHIR-20483 rejected denormalizing Encounter diagnosis metadata into Condition.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The active Encounter StructureDefinition already defines Encounter.reason and Encounter.diagnosis with the intended reason-versus-addressed-condition semantics, CodeableReference children, repeat use fields per later decisions, and Account-based billing/ranking guidance. The requested use terminology is present, and no Encounter.diagnosis.rank should be restored.
